scope: New discovery pointers only; no projects or records have been copied from these third-party trackers. Descriptions distinguish each resource scope and retain access/claim limitations.

items.name: Decompendium
items.description: A public index of matching game decompilations, grouped by game, with progress sourced from each project’s own CI. The live site describes matching as byte-for-byte reproduction and states that it hosts no code or game data.
items.source_evidence: The maintainer README defines the index as matching decompilations grouped by game, explains CI-derived progress, and links the live site. The homepage was fetched successfully on 2026-10-16 and displayed game/project entries with progress. The repository distinguishes MIT code from CC0 catalog data. Added as an index pointer only; its project list was not copied.

items.name: Recomp
items.description: A live tracker for game and software decompilation, static recompilation, clean-room reconstruction and preservation projects, with console/category browsing, activity and release views.
items.source_evidence: The live homepage describes coverage of decompilation, static recompilation, clean-room and preservation work; it exposes categories, per-platform lists, releases, news and project links. The page was fetched successfully on 2026-10-16. It is distinct from recomp.fyi, which remains separately cataloged. No tracker records were copied.

items.name: decompilati.onl
items.description: A game-decompilation progress tracker where project owners report code/data progress from CI. The checked homepage exposed three projects and describes matching, partial matching, data progress, project areas, history and community votes; it does not present itself as a general recompilation index.
items.source_evidence: The official repository README documents owner registration and CI/webhook reporting, matching and partial matching progress, data reports, project history and community votes. The live homepage was fetched successfully on 2026-10-16 and showed three listed projects plus a link from decomp.dev. Its narrower decompilation-only scope is retained here. No tracker records were copied.

items.name: ByteMatch
items.description: An open-source matching-decompilation progress tracker that ingests objdiff CI reports and provides project pages, unit maps, history, badges, an API and GitHub pull-request comments. Its maintainer README presents it as a decomp.dev successor with history import.
items.source_evidence: The official repository README documents ingestion of objdiff reports, progress pages/history/badges/API, GitHub pull-request comments, migration of decomp.dev history, and GPL-3.0 licensing. The public site was fetched successfully on 2026-10-16. GitHub metadata showed an active, non-archived repository last pushed 2026-10-15. Added as a discovery pointer only; no project records were copied.

items.name: PC Master Race Latinoamérica native PC port / recomp / decomp list
items.description: A community-published reference page for native PC ports, recompilations and decompilations. Its publisher’s X post on 2026-10-16 says the list had 300+ new or updated entries and added required ROM/ISO/PKG filenames or specific game versions where available. The linked article returned HTTP 403 during review, so its contents and count could not be inspected independently.
items.source_evidence: The publisher’s X post links to this article and self-reports a major update with 300+ new/updated entries and more specific file/version requirements. X’s public page returned the post text on 2026-10-16. The linked PCMR article returned HTTP 403, so this is listed only as a clearly qualified discovery pointer; neither the 300+ figure nor the article contents are independently verified.
